question:
(a) Compare series and parallel combinations of identical cells in terms of equivalent emf and equivalent internal resistance.
(b) Two identical cells, each of emf $1.5\,\text{V}$ and internal resistance $0.5\,\Omega$, are connected first in series and then in parallel. Calculate the equivalent emf and equivalent internal resistance in each case.
(c) Which combination is more suitable when the external resistance is very small? Give reason.

options.A:
(a) For $n$ identical cells, series gives $\varepsilon_s=\varepsilon$, $r_s=r/n$; parallel gives $\varepsilon_p=n\varepsilon$, $r_p=nr$.
(b) Series: $1.5\,\text{V},0.25\,\Omega$; parallel: $3.0\,\text{V},1.0\,\Omega$.
(c) Series is best for very small external resistance.
options.B:
(a) Series: $\varepsilon_s=n\varepsilon$, $r_s=nr$; parallel: $\varepsilon_p=\varepsilon$, $r_p=\dfrac{r}{n}$.
(b) For two cells, series gives $3.0\,\text{V},1.0\,\Omega$; parallel gives $1.5\,\text{V},0.25\,\Omega$.
(c) Parallel is suitable for very small external resistance because it reduces effective internal resistance and supplies larger current.
options.C:
(a) Series and parallel connections have the same equivalent emf and internal resistance.
(b) Both give $3.0\,\text{V},1.0\,\Omega$.
(c) Either combination is equally suitable.
options.D:
(a) Series increases emf but makes internal resistance zero; parallel increases both emf and internal resistance.
(b) Series: $3.0\,\text{V},0\,\Omega$; parallel: $3.0\,\text{V},0.5\,\Omega$.
(c) Series is suitable for small external resistance.
